examples.en: These days, the same work keeps getting easier.
Prices keep going up, and it worries me.

examples.ko: 갈수록 날씨가 추워지니까 두꺼운 옷을 사야겠어요.
examples.en: It's getting colder day by day, so I should buy thick clothes.

examples.ko: 아이들이 갈수록 키가 커서 옷이 금방 작아져요.
examples.en: The children grow taller and taller, so their clothes get small quickly.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 갈수록 살기 좋아지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: This neighbourhood seems to be getting better to live in.

explain: 갈수록은 ‘시간이 지날수록’이라는 뜻으로 혼자서도 써요. 좋은 변화에도, 나쁜 변화에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 갈수록 더 큰 산이 나오는 것처럼 어려운 일이 점점 커질 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: a proverb: like mountains getting bigger as you go, difficulties keep growing

dict_examples.en: People's attitudes are getting harsher and harsher.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Environmental pollution is getting worse and worse.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The symptoms got worse day by day.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 여성의 사회 진출이 갈수록 활발해지고 있다.
dict_examples.en: Women's participation in society is becoming increasingly active.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 갈수록 can stand alone and means “as time goes on”. You can use it for good changes and bad changes.

examples.en: On days when I'm tired, my concentration drops.
Coffee helps me concentrate.

examples.ko: 휴대폰을 끄면 집중력을 높일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you turn off your phone, you can improve your concentration.

examples.ko: 아이들은 집중력이 오래가지 않아서 수업을 짧게 나눠요.
examples.en: Children can't hold their concentration for long, so we split the class into short parts.
In a noisy cafe, my concentration gets scattered.

explain: 집중력은 ‘집중’에 ‘력(힘)’이 붙은 말이에요. 이해력, 기억력, 체력도 같은 방식이에요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 적당한 실내 온도는 공부할 때 집중력을 높여 준다.
dict_examples.en: A comfortable room temperature improves concentration when studying.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 동생은 집중력이 모자라 책상 앞에 오래 앉아 있지를 못한다.
dict_examples.en: My younger sibling lacks concentration and can't sit at a desk for long.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 집중력 is 집중 plus 력 (power). 이해력, 기억력 and 체력 are built the same way.

examples.en: Autumn is gradually deepening.

examples.ko: 같이 일할수록 두 사람의 대화가 깊어졌어요.
examples.en: The more the two of them worked together, the deeper their conversations became.
As autumn deepens, the weather is getting chillier.
As the night grew deep, the street became quiet.

examples.ko: 오래 만나면서 두 사람의 정이 깊어졌어요.
examples.en: Over time, the two people's affection grew deeper.
The closer the exam gets, the deeper my worries grow.

explain: ‘깊다’ + ‘-어지다’가 ‘깊어지다’예요. 반대는 ‘얕아지다’예요. 밤, 정, 고민, 생각에 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 작은 오해 때문에 두 사람 사이에 갈등의 골이 깊어졌어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 나빠진 정도가 깊은 골짜기처럼 커질 때 써요. 뉴스에서도 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when a relationship worsens, like a valley getting deeper; often heard in the news

dict_examples.ko: 졸업할 때가 되면서 졸업 후에 무엇을 할지 고민이 깊어졌다.
dict_examples.en: As graduation approached, my worries about what to do afterward deepened.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Everyday; night, affection, worry or thought gets deeper naturally. 깊다 + -어지다 makes 깊어지다 (to become deeper). The opposite is 얕아지다. It goes with night, affection, worry and thought.

t90.ax: As the night grew deep, the street became quiet.

examples.en: The closer we got, the easier it became to ask questions.
If you don't know something, ask your teacher.
I raised my hand and asked a question during class.
After the meeting, I asked about what I wondered.
I was too shy to ask a question.

explain: 말할 때는 ‘물어보다’를 더 많이 쓰고, ‘질문하다’는 수업, 회의, 발표처럼 조금 공식적인 자리에 잘 어울려요. 묻는 상대는 ‘에게’, 윗사람이면 ‘께’를 써요. 질문을 듣는 쪽은 ‘질문을 받다’라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 국회 의원이 교육감에게 교육 분야의 현안과 관련된 내용을 질문했다.
dict_examples.en: A National Assembly member asked the superintendent of education questions about current issues in education.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: In everyday speech '물어보다' is more common; '질문하다' suits more formal settings like classes, meetings and presentations. Mark the person asked with '에게', or '께' for a superior. The person being asked '질문을 받다'.

t90.ax: I was too shy to ask a question.

en: to be huge; to be enormous; to be gigantic

examples.en: A giant tree watches over the village.
Whales are truly enormous.
The waves were huge, so I was scared.
I was amazed at the hugely built building.
That company grew into a giant enterprise.
It was much bigger than it looked in photos.

explain: '거대하다'는 '크다'보다 훨씬 커서 놀랄 정도일 때 써요. 건물, 동물, 산, 기업처럼 눈에 띄게 큰 것에 잘 어울려요. 작은 물건이나 사람의 키에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: There is a huge building in the middle of the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요. 건물, 산, 동물에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun; fits buildings, mountains and animals.

phrases.example: 가까이에서 보니 산이 더 거대해 보여요.
phrases.en: The mountain looks even more enormous up close.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈으로 본 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how something looks to the eye.

phrases.en: That animal is not as huge as I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각보다 크지 않다고 말할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying something is not as big as expected.

explain_en: Enormous in scale — formal, imposing (거대한 나무) 거대하다 is used when something is far bigger than 크다, large enough to be startling. It fits buildings, animals, mountains and companies. It is not used much for small objects or a person's height.

examples.en: My older brother is so good that I feel a sense of rivalry.

examples.ko: 아이들은 놀다가 경쟁심 때문에 싸우기도 해요.
examples.en: Kids sometimes fight over competitiveness while playing.
A moderate amount of competitiveness helps with studying.

examples.ko: 친구에게 경쟁심을 느끼는 건 나쁜 일이 아니에요.
examples.en: Feeling competitive toward a friend is not a bad thing.

examples.ko: 그 둘은 경쟁심이 강해서 늘 내기를 해요.
examples.en: Those two are so competitive that they always make bets.
Burning with the urge to compete, I practiced all night.

explain: '경쟁심이 강하다/생기다/들다'처럼 써요. '승부욕'은 이기고 싶은 마음이고, '경쟁심'은 상대를 의식하는 마음이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 제 동생은 경쟁심이 강해서 지는 것을 싫어해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is very competitive and hates to lose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 설명할 때 쓰는 대표 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical expression for describing someone's personality.

phrases.en: My friend won a prize, so I felt a sense of rivalry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 의식하는 마음이 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you become aware of someone as a rival.

phrases.nuance_ko: 남과 겨루려는 마음이 적다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you have little desire to compete.

explain_en: It appears in phrases like '경쟁심이 강하다/생기다/들다'. '승부욕' is the desire to win, while '경쟁심' leans more toward being conscious of a rival.

examples.en: A big fish got caught on the fishhook.
First, you put the bait on the fishhook.
This fishhook is very sharp, so be careful.
I accidentally pricked my finger on the fishhook.
The tip of the hook was bent, so I replaced it with a new one.

examples.ko: 낚시 가게에서 낚싯바늘을 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pack of fishhooks at the fishing shop.

explain: 물고기가 '낚싯바늘에 걸리다'라고 말하고, 사람이 찔릴 때는 '찔리다'를 써요. '바늘'만 쓰면 바느질 바늘로 들리니까 낚시 얘기에서는 '낚싯바늘'이라고 해요. 낚싯대, 낚싯줄과 같이 낚시 도구로 묶어서 외워요.

phrases.en: I put bait on the hook and cast it.
phrases.nuance_en: What you say when getting ready to fish.
phrases.en_equiv: to put bait on a hook

phrases.en: My finger got pricked by a fishhook.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 찔리다 when a person gets hurt.
phrases.en_equiv: to be pricked by a fishhook

phrases.en: You catch small fish with small hooks.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 작은 to describe size.

explain_en: A fish 'gets caught' on it (낚싯바늘에 걸리다), and a person gets pricked (찔리다). '바늘' alone sounds like a sewing needle, so use '낚싯바늘' when talking about fishing. Learn it together with 낚싯대 and 낚싯줄.

examples.en: When it rained, even the dry land became moist.
Farmers grow grain on the wide land.

examples.ko: 이 집은 대지는 넓은데 건물은 작아요.
examples.en: This house has a large lot, but the building is small.
When spring comes, sprouts come up from the ground.
The children ran freely across the wide land.
An earthquake struck and the ground shook hard.

explain: 대지는 넓게 펼쳐진 땅을 글 같은 느낌으로 부르는 말이라서 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 보통 '땅'이라고 해요. 건물을 짓는 땅은 '대지 면적'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The ground got wet because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, '땅' is much more common than '대지'.

phrases.en: I can see wide land outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓게 펼쳐진 땅을 글 같은 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat literary way to describe wide, open land.

phrases.en: This house has a large lot area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물을 짓는 땅의 크기를 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the size of the land a building stands on.

explain_en: Literary word for broad land or earth, poetic and written. 대지 is a literary way to call wide stretches of land, so you see it in news and writing. In everyday speech people usually say '땅'. For a plot of land for a building, it appears as in '대지 면적' (lot area).

t90.ax: Farmers grow grain on the wide land.

examples.en: The more I learn Korean, the more fun it gets.
The more I practice the same sentence, the fewer mistakes I make.
This program gets easier the more you use it.
The more you read the same text, the deeper your understanding gets.
The better we get to know each other, the easier it is to talk.
The harder the problem, the more slowly I read the explanation.

explain: -(으)ㄹ수록 뒤에는 ‘더’나 ‘점점’을 자주 붙여요. 뒤 문장은 보통 변화를 말해요. 예를 들어 ‘더 쉬워져요’처럼요.
explain_en: After -(으)ㄹ수록, people often add 더 or 점점. The second part usually describes a change, such as 더 쉬워져요 (it gets easier).
